subsystems.name: UV-capable space telescope
subsystems.role: collects ultraviolet light, which the atmosphere blocks from the ground, so the instrument must be in orbit.
parts: primary and secondary mirrors with UV-reflective coatings

subsystems.name: Starlight suppression
subsystems.role: separates the faint planet signal from a star billions of times brighter.
parts: coronagraph optics or an external starshade

subsystems.name: UV spectrograph
subsystems.role: spreads light so the depth of the ozone Hartley absorption band (roughly 200-300 nm, strongest near 255 nm) can be measured.

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: counts individual ultraviolet photons with low noise.
parts: photon-counting microchannel plate or UV-optimised CCD

subsystems.name: Observatory operations
subsystems.role: keeps pointing and thermal conditions stable across dozens of repeated transits.

subsystems.name: Interpretation pipeline
subsystems.role: turns spectra into a judgement about an oxygen-rich atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Pick the spectral window
buildSteps.detail: Design the instrument around the ozone Hartley band near 250 nm, where absorption is strong but stellar noise and interstellar extinction must be modelled.

buildSteps.title: Make ultraviolet optics
buildSteps.detail: Polish mirror blanks to nanometre smoothness and apply aluminium coatings protected by thin magnesium fluoride or lithium fluoride layers to preserve ultraviolet reflectivity.

buildSteps.title: Design starlight suppression
buildSteps.detail: If the goal is reflected-light detection rather than transit spectroscopy, build a coronagraph or a precisely shaped starshade and show in a vacuum testbed that it reaches the contrast needed.

buildSteps.title: Build the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: Align the slit, grating and optics so the ozone band lands on the detector with enough resolving power to separate it from neighbouring molecular features.

buildSteps.title: Integrate a photon-counting detector
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the sealed detector, verify its quantum efficiency in the ultraviolet and shield it from stray light.

buildSteps.title: Vacuum and thermal test
buildSteps.detail: Run the whole payload in a space-environment chamber to confirm alignment, focus and background levels hold across the temperature swings of orbit.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: Deploy the observatory, then spend months calibrating wavelength scale, throughput and scattered light before science observations begin.

buildSteps.title: Observe and co-add
buildSteps.detail: Record many transits or eclipse events of the same target, then stack the data to push noise down to the level of the faint ozone signal.

buildSteps.title: Interpret with a redox budget
buildSteps.detail: Combine the measured ozone column with methane abundance, carbon dioxide and the planet's energy balance in models to weigh biological against abiotic explanations.

prerequisites.why: ultraviolet light does not reach the ground, and few space observatories with the needed spectrographs remain or are funded.
coronagraphy and starshade performance have not been demonstrated in space at the contrast ultraviolet observations would demand.
photon-counting detectors and protected aluminium coatings are established technology, though efficiency remains modest.
abiotic routes such as runaway greenhouse water loss or carbon dioxide photolysis can build up oxygen, and the models are still being tested.
the signal is a fraction of a percent deep, so pointing and instrument drift must be controlled across many repeat visits.

pathway.milestone: ultraviolet transit spectroscopy of a handful of gas-rich planets, plus Earthshine spectra recorded during lunar eclipses as a known-life benchmark
pathway.unlocks: proof that ozone and related features can be measured in a planetary spectrum.

pathway.milestone: dedicated ultraviolet spectrographs on new space observatories with improved stability
pathway.unlocks: ozone screening for small planets around quiet, cool stars where the band is relatively strong.

pathway.milestone: a large space telescope with an ultraviolet channel and a demonstrated coronagraph or starshade
pathway.unlocks: reflected-light spectra of rocky planets, not just transiting ones.

pathway.milestone: a systematic survey of nearby rocky worlds combining ozone, methane and redox budgets
pathway.unlocks: a statistical rather than anecdotal search for oxygen-rich atmospheres.
